title: Resource claims model and explicit-deny priority for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and spec work for a new RBAC v2 role model focusing on: 1) an explicit "resource claims" abstraction that decouples actor capabilities from resource tenancy, 2) an explicit-deny precedence model for emergency breakglass and revocations, 3) a compact permissions matrix that supports inheritance across resource hierarchies, and 4) audit hooks and SAML/SSO attribute mappings required for private deployments. This ticket produces a design doc, compatibility matrix for current roles, and a migration plan for runtime enforcement and audit logging integration.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical JSON schema for resource claims, scopes, and bindings exists and is reviewed by Security and Platform
Explicit-deny evaluation order defined with test vectors (conflicting allow/deny across multiple role bindings)
Permissions matrix covering common resources (workspace, model, deployment, billing, audit) with inheritance examples is published
SAML attribute mapping proposal (groups / role claims / session attributes) documented and example SAML responses included
Audit event contract specified: events for bind/unbind, role-update, breakglass activation, and evaluation failures; downstream log schema validated with Observability team
Migration plan: strategy for legacy role resolution compatibility, rollout windows, and canary checks for Dedicated/Private tenants
implementation_notes: Introduce 'claim' objects: {subject, resource_namespace, scope_set, ttl, origin} stored as first-class entities for fast evaluation
Evaluation pipeline: collect principal attributes (SAML/SSO), expand derived claims, resolve explicit-deny, evaluate allow rules, apply breakglass overrides, emit audit events
Precedence: explicit-deny > breakglass-disable > scoped-allow > wildcard-allow; documented with prioritized rule list
KV cache considerations: cache resolved claims per session key; invalidate on role change events via pub/sub
Runtime contract: provide evaluation API with 'explain' mode returning applied bindings and decision trace for use by Console and incident investigations
